commit_message:
Integrate LLVM to llvm/llvm-project@a938559a9145 (#24982)

Updates LLVM to llvm/llvm-project@a938559a9145, retaining the GPU
min/maxnumf carry patch from llvm/llvm-project#226903.

Compatibility changes:

- Bump StableHLO to openxla/stablehlo@c2eaf28a to pick up compatibility
with strict property assembly formats (llvm/llvm-project@c495a9b796c4).
  Upstream also covers these previously carried IREE fixes:
  - Migrate complex element handling to `mlir::Complex`
    (iree-org/stablehlo@28549ef5).
  - Remove obsolete DenseMap empty/tombstone key handling
    (iree-org/stablehlo@a2727e57).
  - Preserve enum assembly syntax without angle brackets
    (iree-org/stablehlo@50a9d75a).
- Temporarily opt affected IREE dialects and Torch-MLIR TMTensor out of
  strict property assembly formats to preserve existing syntax
  (llvm/llvm-project@c495a9b796c4).
- Replace `checkParallelRegions` with `mayHaveParallelRegions`,
preserving
  existing bufferization behavior (llvm/llvm-project@d6048f5ff3bd).
- Use DataLayout-aware constant GEP construction in LLVMCPU
  (llvm/llvm-project@2a6247359ee5).
- Keep widening visible through shape casts for CPU custom kernels and
  SPIR-V dot products after (llvm/llvm-project@2c298348bfe1)
- Update the TOSA constant check for its new assembly format
  (llvm/llvm-project@fe5ace607b58)
- Carry the MMA slice-cache correction for the regression introduced 
  by (llvm/llvm-project@d287e55d0302)

Assisted-by: Codex

Compatibility changes:

- Bump StableHLO to openxla/stablehlo@c2eaf28a to pick up compatibility
with strict property assembly formats (llvm/llvm-project@c495a9b796c4).
  Upstream also covers these previously carried IREE fixes:
  - Migrate complex element handling to `mlir::Complex`
    (iree-org/stablehlo@28549ef5).
  - Remove obsolete DenseMap empty/tombstone key handling
    (iree-org/stablehlo@a2727e57).
  - Preserve enum assembly syntax without angle brackets
    (iree-org/stablehlo@50a9d75a).
- Temporarily opt affected IREE dialects and Torch-MLIR TMTensor out of
  strict property assembly formats to preserve existing syntax
  (llvm/llvm-project@c495a9b796c4).
- Replace `checkParallelRegions` with `mayHaveParallelRegions`,
preserving
  existing bufferization behavior (llvm/llvm-project@d6048f5ff3bd).
- Use DataLayout-aware constant GEP construction in LLVMCPU
  (llvm/llvm-project@2a6247359ee5).
- Keep widening visible through shape casts for CPU custom kernels and
  SPIR-V dot products after (llvm/llvm-project@2c298348bfe1)
- Update the TOSA constant check for its new assembly format
  (llvm/llvm-project@fe5ace607b58)
- Carry the MMA slice-cache correction for the regression introduced 
  by (llvm/llvm-project@d287e55d0302)

Assisted-by: Codex

commit_message:
[Integrate] Update torch-mlir to 528d3dcb

Update to upstream torch-mlir through 528d3dcb, using the IREE
integration revision adapted to the current LLVM pin.

The new range fixes several ONNX op tests, so drop them from the
expected run failures of the CI-exercised configs:
averagepool_3d_dilations_large_count_include_pad_is_0_ceil_mode_is_True,
nonmaxsuppression_flipped_coordinates, and
reduce_{max,min}_bool_inputs.

test_reversesequence_time now fails to compile on llvm-cpu.
ReverseSequence lowers to an scf.for over the time axis, so each
dispatch reverses a column selected by a dynamic offset. The resulting
vector.gather reads a strided column subview with a dynamic offset:
RemoveStrideFromGatherSource bails on the dynamic offset and
Gather1DToConditionalLoads rejects the non-unit inner stride, leaving
the gather for LLVM conversion. Mark it as an expected compile failure
until the MLIR gather lowering handles dynamic subview offsets.

Signed-off-by: Thomas Ziereis <ziereis@roofline.ai>
name: setup / setup

the gather for LLVM conversion. Mark it as an expected compile failure
until the MLIR gather lowering handles dynamic subview offsets.

commit_message:
Integrate LLVM to llvm/llvm-project@a938559a9145 (#24982)

Updates LLVM to llvm/llvm-project@a938559a9145, retaining the GPU
min/maxnumf carry patch from llvm/llvm-project#226903.

Compatibility changes:

- Bump StableHLO to openxla/stablehlo@c2eaf28a to pick up compatibility
with strict property assembly formats (llvm/llvm-project@c495a9b796c4).
  Upstream also covers these previously carried IREE fixes:
  - Migrate complex element handling to `mlir::Complex`
    (iree-org/stablehlo@28549ef5).
  - Remove obsolete DenseMap empty/tombstone key handling
    (iree-org/stablehlo@a2727e57).
  - Preserve enum assembly syntax without angle brackets
    (iree-org/stablehlo@50a9d75a).
- Temporarily opt affected IREE dialects and Torch-MLIR TMTensor out of
  strict property assembly formats to preserve existing syntax
  (llvm/llvm-project@c495a9b796c4).
- Replace `checkParallelRegions` with `mayHaveParallelRegions`,
preserving
  existing bufferization behavior (llvm/llvm-project@d6048f5ff3bd).
- Use DataLayout-aware constant GEP construction in LLVMCPU
  (llvm/llvm-project@2a6247359ee5).
- Keep widening visible through shape casts for CPU custom kernels and
  SPIR-V dot products after (llvm/llvm-project@2c298348bfe1)
- Update the TOSA constant check for its new assembly format
  (llvm/llvm-project@fe5ace607b58)
- Carry the MMA slice-cache correction for the regression introduced 
  by (llvm/llvm-project@d287e55d0302)

Assisted-by: Codex

---------

Signed-off-by: Jelle Schühmacher <schuehmacher@roofline.ai>

Bzlmod consumers may embed IREE under a different path or repository
name. Resolving IREE-owned targets and bundled sources in the

for the consumer.
    
The following PR adds the use of Labels(..) so those references
can stay attached to IREE while consumer-provided

commit_message:
[VM] Preserve 64-bit values in internal calls (#24946)

Internal calls marshaled one 32-bit register per argument and result, so
the high word of a 64-bit value was dropped or overwritten by the next
argument. When that value feeds a buffer bound it surfaces in HAL
command buffer validation as an out-of-range binding, as seen in #24929.

Marshal each argument and result at its full width from the callee's
calling convention, and align argument registers to match how external
calls and imports are already marshaled.

Adds call_ops.vmasm cases for consecutive i64 arguments, i64 results,
and mixed primitive/ref calls. The full VM bytecode test suite passes,
and the repro from #24929, which aborted with OUT_OF_RANGE before the
fix, now returns the expected output.

Fixes #24929

commit_message:
[Bindings][Compiler] Add Bazel support for Python bindings

IREE's compiler Python support is available through CMake, but its generated
dialect bindings, native extensions and compiler tool wrappers are not exposed
as Bazel targets. Downstream projects using Bazel therefore need to maintain
their own build definitions to package Python bindings that match the compiler
they build.

Providing these targets upstream lets consumers build Python compiler packages
against their chosen IREE revision and keeps the binding definitions alongside
the sources they describe. The bindings use `IREECompiler`'s shared C API so
Python code can inspect and construct IR, then invoke the compiler using the
same MLIR implementation. Consumers retain control of package and wheel assembly.

commit_message:
fix(PackConstants): don't start new storage buffer if current one is still empty (#23927)

The PackConstants pass introduces a new buffer when a constant cannot be
packed into the current buffer without exceeding the maximum size.
However, if a constant is itself larger than the limit, it gets still
added, but in a separate buffer.
This change fixes a bug in the packing logic when a constant bigger than
the limit is encountered when the current buffer is still empty. In this
case, the current buffer stayed empty and the big constant got added to
a new buffer. The empty buffer caused errors of size 0 buffers not being
supported in following passes or in the runtime. This change avoids
adding a new buffer is the current one is empty and thus avoids these
errors.

commit_message:
[Bazel] use execution paths for genrule inputs

IREE's shared genrule definitions use rootpath for source files and
execpath for generated files so CMake can distinguish source and build
directories. In Bazel, however, rootpath describes runtime runfiles paths,
which break external IREE builds without legacy runfiles. Translate these
to execpath in the Bazel macro so build actions can locate their inputs.
Existing standalone IREE rules and CMake behavior remain unchanged.

commit_message:
[CI] Add RDNA3 and RDNA4 Vulkan e2e tests under rocjitsu

Add CPU-hosted Vulkan compute e2e coverage for gfx1100 and gfx1201 in
the Linux x64 Clang job. Reuse the existing SPIR-V modules and let Mesa
RADV compile them to each simulated GPU's native instructions.

Install Mesa RADV from the Kisak turtle PPA and share one TheRock SDK
pinned to 10.2.0a20261002 between HIP and Vulkan. Use its Mirage launcher
with in-process simulation and eight parallel CTest workers.

Verify the RADV driver and simulated PCI device identity before running
CTest. Set both Vulkan ICD selectors for Jammy's loader, use a 60-minute
Vulkan step timeout, and retain per-target logs and JUnit results. Run
Vulkan after HIP failures when dependency installation succeeds.

Assisted-by: codex

Add CPU-hosted Vulkan compute e2e coverage for gfx1100 and gfx1201 in
the Linux x64 Clang job. Reuse the existing SPIR-V modules and let Mesa
RADV compile them to each simulated GPU's native instructions.

Install Mesa RADV from the Kisak turtle PPA and share one TheRock SDK
pinned to 10.2.0a20261002 between HIP and Vulkan. Use its Mirage launcher
with in-process simulation and eight parallel CTest workers.

Verify the RADV driver and simulated PCI device identity before running
CTest. Set both Vulkan ICD selectors for Jammy's loader, use a 60-minute
Vulkan step timeout, and retain per-target logs and JUnit results. Run
Vulkan after HIP failures when dependency installation succeeds.

Assisted-by: codex
name: Test RISC-V 64 / riscv64

[CI] Add RDNA3 and RDNA4 Vulkan e2e tests under rocjitsu

Add CPU-hosted Vulkan compute e2e coverage for gfx1100 and gfx1201 in
the Linux x64 Clang job. Reuse the existing SPIR-V modules and let Mesa
RADV compile them to each simulated GPU's native instructions.

Install Mesa RADV from the Kisak turtle PPA and pin the Vulkan TheRock
SDK to 10.2.0a20261002. Use the SDK's Mirage launcher with in-process
simulation and eight parallel CTest workers.

Verify the RADV driver and simulated PCI device identity before running
CTest. Set both Vulkan ICD selectors for Jammy's loader, apply per-test
and per-session timeouts, and retain per-target logs and JUnit results.

Keep the existing HIP SDK pin while numerical failures with the newer
runtime are investigated.

Assisted-by: codex

commit_message:
[iree-benchmark-module] Unify sync, async and dispatch execution

iree-benchmark-module had separate synchronous, asynchronous and
generated-dispatch execution paths that applied output processing,
replay capture and profiling flushes inconsistently. Run all of them
through one batch lifecycle, so discovery resolves each function's ABI
and iteration accounting once and every path shares the measured loop.

This fixes bugs of the separate paths:
- Asynchronous outputs are retained for --enable_output_processing.
- Discovered asynchronous functions get their fence arguments instead of
  failing without a message.
- Dispatch benchmarks selected with --function get their repeat count.
- Non-power-of-two --batch_concurrency no longer reads past the
  invocation list.
- Asynchronous replay captures work because context setup returns the
  recording devices that fences must be created on.

Behavior changes:
- Errors go to stderr with EXIT_FAILURE, as in iree-run-module, instead
  of stdout with the status code as the exit code.
- --enable_output_processing needs a single benchmarked function instead
  of silently processing nothing.
- Nonpositive --batch_size and --batch_concurrency are rejected.

The lifecycle tests run the tool through iree.runtime.benchmark.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
name: Analyze (python)

commit_message:
[iree-benchmark-module] Add dispatch timing rows

Add --dispatch_statistics for a per-function breakdown of where a
benchmark spends its dispatch time. After each measured repetition,
Google Benchmark reruns the registered benchmark outside the measured
interval with a lightweight HAL statistics session on every device, so
profiling uses the same function ABI, batch accounting and asynchronous
concurrency as measurement. The rows appear under their benchmark in
console, JSON and CSV output, including --benchmark_out files, whose
formatter is selected from Google Benchmark's parsed flags. Conflicting
profiling, capture and replay flags are rejected before any session
starts or the replay file is opened.

To start sessions with explicit options, the tooling profiling session
type is now iree_hal_profiling_session_t with _begin, _flush and _end
functions, and iree_hal_profiling_from_flags_is_requested validates the
profiling flags without starting a session. The device profiling flags
of iree-benchmark-module now cover every device instead of the first.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit_message:
Integrate LLVM to llvm/llvm-project@a938559a9145 (#24982)

Updates LLVM to llvm/llvm-project@a938559a9145, retaining the GPU
min/maxnumf carry patch from llvm/llvm-project#226903.

Compatibility changes:

- Bump StableHLO to openxla/stablehlo@c2eaf28a to pick up compatibility
with strict property assembly formats (llvm/llvm-project@c495a9b796c4).
  Upstream also covers these previously carried IREE fixes:
  - Migrate complex element handling to `mlir::Complex`
    (iree-org/stablehlo@28549ef5).
  - Remove obsolete DenseMap empty/tombstone key handling
    (iree-org/stablehlo@a2727e57).
  - Preserve enum assembly syntax without angle brackets
    (iree-org/stablehlo@50a9d75a).
- Temporarily opt affected IREE dialects and Torch-MLIR TMTensor out of
  strict property assembly formats to preserve existing syntax
  (llvm/llvm-project@c495a9b796c4).
- Replace `checkParallelRegions` with `mayHaveParallelRegions`,
preserving
  existing bufferization behavior (llvm/llvm-project@d6048f5ff3bd).
- Use DataLayout-aware constant GEP construction in LLVMCPU
  (llvm/llvm-project@2a6247359ee5).
- Keep widening visible through shape casts for CPU custom kernels and
  SPIR-V dot products after (llvm/llvm-project@2c298348bfe1)
- Update the TOSA constant check for its new assembly format
  (llvm/llvm-project@fe5ace607b58)
- Carry the MMA slice-cache correction for the regression introduced 
  by (llvm/llvm-project@d287e55d0302)

Assisted-by: Codex

---------

Signed-off-by: Jelle Schühmacher <schuehmacher@roofline.ai>

commit_message:
[Integrate] Update torch-mlir to 528d3dcb

Update to upstream torch-mlir through 528d3dcb, using the IREE
integration revision adapted to the current LLVM pin.

The new range fixes several ONNX op tests, so drop them from the
expected run failures of the CI-exercised configs:
averagepool_3d_dilations_large_count_include_pad_is_0_ceil_mode_is_True,
nonmaxsuppression_flipped_coordinates, and
reduce_{max,min}_bool_inputs.

test_reversesequence_time now fails to compile on llvm-cpu.
ReverseSequence lowers to an scf.for over the time axis, so each
dispatch reverses a column selected by a dynamic offset. The resulting
vector.gather reads a strided column subview with a dynamic offset:
RemoveStrideFromGatherSource bails on the dynamic offset and
Gather1DToConditionalLoads rejects the non-unit inner stride, leaving
the gather for LLVM conversion. Mark it as an expected compile failure
until the MLIR gather lowering handles dynamic subview offsets.

Signed-off-by: Thomas Ziereis <ziereis@roofline.ai>
name: Test Torch / test_torch_ops :: amdgpu_hip_gfx1100_O3

commit_message:
[CI] Add RDNA3 and RDNA4 Vulkan e2e tests under rocjitsu

Run HIP and Vulkan e2e tests in a dedicated Ubuntu 24.04 job using official
Mesa RADV packages. Reuse the existing SPIR-V modules for gfx1100 and
gfx1201 and let RADV compile them to the simulated GPU's instructions.

Share TheRock SDK 10.2.0a20261002 between both suites. Temporarily build
rocjitsu at f21f78dc78ae until a wheel includes the SDMA count fix from
https://github.com/ROCm/rocm-systems/pull/12708.

Verify the RADV driver and simulated PCI device identity before CTest.
Use eight test workers, a 60-minute Vulkan step timeout, and per-target
logs and JUnit results. Run Vulkan even when HIP tests fail.

Order PluginABIHash.h generation before consumers in child directories
compile, fixing a missing dependency exposed by the fresh build.

Assisted-by: codex
name: setup / setup

commit_message:
[CI] Add RDNA3 and RDNA4 Vulkan e2e tests under rocjitsu

Run HIP and Vulkan e2e tests in a dedicated Ubuntu 24.04 job using official
Mesa RADV packages. Reuse the existing SPIR-V modules for gfx1100 and
gfx1201 and let RADV compile them to the simulated GPU's instructions.

Share TheRock SDK 10.2.0a20261002 between both suites. Temporarily build
rocjitsu at f21f78dc78ae until a wheel includes the SDMA count fix from
https://github.com/ROCm/rocm-systems/pull/12708.

Verify the RADV driver and simulated PCI device identity before CTest.
Use eight test workers, a 60-minute Vulkan step timeout, and per-target
logs and JUnit results. Run Vulkan even when HIP tests fail.

Order PluginABIHash.h generation before consumers in child directories
compile, fixing a missing dependency exposed by the fresh build.

commit_message:
[CI] Add RDNA3 and RDNA4 Vulkan e2e tests under rocjitsu

Run HIP and Vulkan e2e tests in a dedicated Ubuntu 24.04 job using official
Mesa RADV packages. Reuse the existing SPIR-V modules for gfx1100 and
gfx1201 and let RADV compile them to the simulated GPU's instructions.

Share TheRock SDK 10.2.0a20261002 between both suites. Temporarily build
rocjitsu at f21f78dc78ae until a wheel includes the SDMA count fix from
https://github.com/ROCm/rocm-systems/pull/12708.

Verify the RADV driver and simulated PCI device identity before CTest.
Use eight test workers, a 60-minute Vulkan step timeout, and per-target
logs and JUnit results. Run Vulkan even when HIP tests fail.

Order PluginABIHash.h generation before consumers in child directories
compile, fixing a missing dependency exposed by the fresh build.

commit_message:
[Integrate] Update torch-mlir to 528d3dcb

Update to upstream torch-mlir through 528d3dcb, using the IREE
integration revision adapted to the current LLVM pin.

The new range fixes several ONNX op tests, so drop them from the
expected run failures of the CI-exercised configs:
averagepool_3d_dilations_large_count_include_pad_is_0_ceil_mode_is_True,
nonmaxsuppression_flipped_coordinates, and
reduce_{max,min}_bool_inputs.

test_reversesequence_time now fails to compile on llvm-cpu.
ReverseSequence lowers to an scf.for over the time axis, so each
dispatch reverses a column selected by a dynamic offset. The resulting
vector.gather reads a strided column subview with a dynamic offset:
RemoveStrideFromGatherSource bails on the dynamic offset and
Gather1DToConditionalLoads rejects the non-unit inner stride, leaving
the gather for LLVM conversion. Mark it as an expected compile failure
until the MLIR gather lowering handles dynamic subview offsets.

Signed-off-by: Thomas Ziereis <ziereis@roofline.ai>
name: Test Torch / test_torch_ops :: amdgpu_hip_gfx1100_O3

commit_message:
[CI] Add RDNA3 and RDNA4 Vulkan e2e tests under rocjitsu

Add CPU-hosted Vulkan compute e2e coverage for gfx1100 and gfx1201 in
the Linux x64 Clang job. Reuse the existing SPIR-V modules and let Mesa
RADV compile them to each simulated GPU's native instructions.

Install Mesa RADV from the Kisak turtle PPA and share one TheRock SDK
pinned to 10.2.0a20261002 between HIP and Vulkan. Use its Mirage launcher
with in-process simulation and eight parallel CTest workers.

Verify the RADV driver and simulated PCI device identity before running
CTest. Set both Vulkan ICD selectors for Jammy's loader, use a 60-minute
Vulkan step timeout, and retain per-target logs and JUnit results. Run
Vulkan after HIP failures when dependency installation succeeds.

Assisted-by: codex
name: Test ONNX / test_onnx_models :: amdgpu_hip_rdna3

commit_message:
[Integrate] Update torch-mlir to 528d3dcb

Update to upstream torch-mlir through 528d3dcb, using the IREE
integration revision adapted to the current LLVM pin.

The new range fixes several ONNX op tests, so drop them from the
expected run failures of the CI-exercised configs:
averagepool_3d_dilations_large_count_include_pad_is_0_ceil_mode_is_True,
nonmaxsuppression_flipped_coordinates, and
reduce_{max,min}_bool_inputs.

test_reversesequence_time now fails to compile on llvm-cpu.
ReverseSequence lowers to an scf.for over the time axis, so each
dispatch reverses a column selected by a dynamic offset. The resulting
vector.gather reads a strided column subview with a dynamic offset:
RemoveStrideFromGatherSource bails on the dynamic offset and
Gather1DToConditionalLoads rejects the non-unit inner stride, leaving
the gather for LLVM conversion. Mark it as an expected compile failure
until the MLIR gather lowering handles dynamic subview offsets.

Signed-off-by: Thomas Ziereis <ziereis@roofline.ai>
name: Test Torch / test_torch_ops :: amdgpu_hip_gfx1100_O3
